newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Tuesday on short-covering, traders said.
But the most actively traded January 1998 contract ended at 3,327 yuan ($401) per tonne, losing 13 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,328 and hit a low of 3,325 yuan per tonne.
The July 1997 contract rose 30 to 3,280, September 31 to 3,319, November 49 to 3,347 and the March 1998 five to 3,370.
Combined volume rose to 17,700 tonnes from 16,600 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly higher and moved at high levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Short-covering was responsible for today's gains but the mid-term trend was still unclear," one trader said.
"A lack of market-moving news will see soybeans moving in a narrow range in the next few days," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in the short term.
